dashboard.name: Transformations
dashboard.description: Before/after side-by-side for each supported transform: filter, sort, groupBy, calculatedColumn, renameColumns, limit.

chartOptions.content:
## SQL: `WHERE`

Drops rows that don't match a predicate. The raw query returns everything; the filtered widget applies the predicate in the query itself.

**Shown:** `WHERE total >= 300` over the first 100 orders.

widgets.query: SELECT o.id, o.status, o.total::float AS total, c.name AS customer FROM neoboard_demo_public.orders o JOIN neoboard_demo_public.customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id ORDER BY o.id LIMIT 100

SELECT * FROM (SELECT o.id, o.status, o.total::float AS total, c.name AS customer FROM neoboard_demo_public.orders o JOIN neoboard_demo_public.customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id ORDER BY o.id LIMIT 100) first_100 WHERE total >= 300 ORDER BY id

chartOptions.content:
## SQL: `ORDER BY`

Reorders rows by a column, `ASC` or `DESC`. The database sorts the full result, so the order is right whatever the row cap.

**Shown:** `ORDER BY total_spend DESC`.

widgets.query: SELECT c.name AS customer, c.city, SUM(o.total)::float AS total_spend FROM neoboard_demo_public.customers c JOIN neoboard_demo_public.orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY c.id, c.name, c.city

SELECT c.name AS customer, c.city, SUM(o.total)::float AS total_spend FROM neoboard_demo_public.customers c JOIN neoboard_demo_public.orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY c.id, c.name, c.city ORDER BY total_spend DESC, c.id

chartOptions.content:
## SQL: `GROUP BY`

Groups rows by a column and aggregates each group in the database, so a total is never a partial sum of a capped result.

**Shown:**

```sql
SELECT status,
       COUNT(id), SUM(total), AVG(total), MIN(total), MAX(total)
FROM orders
GROUP BY status
```

**Aggregation functions:** `COUNT`, `SUM`, `AVG`, `MIN`, `MAX`.

widgets.query: SELECT id, status, total::float AS total FROM neoboard_demo_public.orders ORDER BY id LIMIT 200

SELECT status, COUNT(id)::int AS id_count, SUM(total)::float AS total_sum, AVG(total)::float AS total_avg, MIN(total)::float AS total_min, MAX(total)::float AS total_max FROM (SELECT id, status, total FROM neoboard_demo_public.orders ORDER BY id LIMIT 200) first_200 GROUP BY status ORDER BY MIN(id)

settings.title: After groupBy status — count + sum/avg/min/max of total

chartOptions.content:
## SQL: a computed column

Adds a column computed from an expression over existing columns.

**Shown:** `(price - cost) AS margin`

Any SQL expression works, not only `+`, `-`, `*` and `/`.

widgets.query: SELECT p.id, p.name AS product, p.price::float AS price, p.cost::float AS cost FROM neoboard_demo_public.products p ORDER BY p.price DESC
SELECT p.id, p.name AS product, p.price::float AS price, p.cost::float AS cost, (p.price - p.cost)::float AS margin FROM neoboard_demo_public.products p ORDER BY p.price DESC, p.id

chartOptions.content:
## SQL: `AS`

Renames columns in the query. Useful for humanizing technical column names in tables, or aligning column names to what a chart type expects (`name` / `value` for pie, `source` / `target` / `value` for sankey).

**Shown:** `name AS "Product", price AS "Price ($)", cost AS "Cost ($)"`

widgets.query: SELECT p.name, p.price::float AS price, p.cost::float AS cost FROM neoboard_demo_public.products p ORDER BY p.price DESC LIMIT 30
SELECT p.name AS "Product", p.price::float AS "Price ($)", p.cost::float AS "Cost ($)" FROM neoboard_demo_public.products p ORDER BY p.price DESC, p.id LIMIT 30

chartOptions.content:
## SQL: `ORDER BY` + `LIMIT`

Caps the row count in the database. Most commonly paired with `ORDER BY` so you get "top N by …".

**Shown:**

```sql
ORDER BY total_spend DESC
LIMIT 5
```

widgets.query: SELECT c.name AS customer, SUM(o.total)::float AS total_spend FROM neoboard_demo_public.customers c JOIN neoboard_demo_public.orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY c.id, c.name

SELECT c.name AS customer, SUM(o.total)::float AS total_spend FROM neoboard_demo_public.customers c JOIN neoboard_demo_public.orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY c.id, c.name ORDER BY total_spend DESC, c.id LIMIT 5

settings.title: After sort desc + limit 5 — top 5 spenders
